events.context: User provides text with music list, travel recommendations, and IELTS advice, requesting extraction of chronological JSON schema of key actions, decisions, and state changes.
System analyzes text to identify core semantic progression, focusing on IELTS-related actions and decisions, ignoring music and travel sections as per constraints.
User decides IELTS certificate (C2 from August 2018) is expired and worthless for PhD applications due to 2-year validity rule.
User determines need for IELTS for UKVI (Academic) test to meet bureaucratic and visa requirements, not for proving English ability.
User plans to book IELTS for UKVI (Academic) in January or February 2026 via British Council or IDP China, costing ~¥2,170.
User decides not to take IELTS tutoring or extensive prep, as current English level (C2 Distinction, academic writing) is sufficient, only needs format familiarization.
User outlines two strategic timing options: Option A (mid-January test for Oxford TAIG March 3 application) or Option B (February test for later applications like Oct 2027).
User recommends Option B (book test for late February 2026) to avoid splitting focus with FAccT paper submission on Jan 13 and because Oxford March 3 is a long shot.
User specifies practical steps: Jan 1 - browse test dates; Jan 2 - book test; Jan 13 - submit FAccT; week before test - spend 2 hours on format familiarization; test day - take test.
User expects IELTS score of 8.5+ overall, with components 8.0-9.0, based on current proficiency, and certificate valid for 2 years through 2027 applications.
